ranking.rationale: Strongest candidate: it directly tests the only positively screened feature family, has full coverage, low leakage and runtime risk, and preserves a clean one-group ablation. The measured +0.00221 lift provides the best available evidence.

Directly aligns training with the within-user ranking objective and has the strongest loss-level expected gain with moderate confidence. It is less evidence-backed than c01 and carries pair-sampling/runtime risk, but remains a focused single-component experiment.

Listwise loss is well aligned with nDCG and offers potentially strong top-ranking gains, but bounded grouping and truncation introduce feasibility and validation risks. Confidence is lower than for BPR.

A focused, low-risk decomposition of the validated request-context signal. Hourmin has plausible mechanism-level value and avoids confounding, though its individual contribution is unmeasured and expected gain is modest.

Clean and inexpensive single-field test of a positively screened feature family. It is useful diagnostically, but tab's isolated contribution is unknown and the expected gain is smaller than the full context group.
Tests a plausible source of conditional context value without adding features, but has only indirect screening evidence, medium runtime risk, and a meaningful sparse interaction overfitting risk.

A reasonably bounded architecture test of missing user-item compatibility, but there is no direct evidence that nonlinear interactions are the bottleneck. Medium runtime and overfitting risk reduce its scarce-experiment value.

Hard negatives could improve top-of-list ordering, but this is dependent on BPR, adds training complexity, and risks noisy or unstable optimization. It also duplicates much of the rationale of the higher-ranked loss experiment.
Low-cost and available at serving time, but date has no isolated positive evidence and may overfit temporal drift. Its expected gain is small and could be negative.
Safe, interpretable decomposition of request context, but weekday is weakly motivated relative to hourmin, has no isolated evidence, and has the lowest expected gain among the context singletons.

Tests personalization of context response, but combines a new crossed representation with a feature change, has medium runtime risk, sparse user-tab parameters, low confidence, and greater validation overfitting risk than simpler context tests.

The only directly measured evidence for this feature group is negative, with a reject recommendation and a negative primary lift. Although feasible and low risk operationally, scarce experimentation should prioritize candidates with positive or at least untested evidence.
